threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it’s weird when you see people bringing their own cups to the local cafés. It’s just a Tuesday here.
Saw a guy serenading the 36 passengers last night with a ukulele. Strangest part? Everyone was actually enjoying it, even the grumpy old man in the back.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The sound of a late-night kebab shop argument spilling onto the street, then switching to a spontaneous jam session. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you sip coffee while listening to live techno at 10 AM on a Sunday. It’s the perfect blend of chill and chaos.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they can still navigate the BART delays like it’s a game, dodging the chaos and catching the next bus without breaking a sweat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, saw a guy serenading Muni passengers with a ukulele while waiting for the 30 bus. Laughter echoed, if only every ride was that lighthearted.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all street performers are charming. But the guy juggling flaming torches on Plaça de la Vila at midnight? Just a fire hazard.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the Gràcia markets; they still think they need to haggle over the price of everything.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look confused trying to figure out the bus stops—it's a rite of passage to miss that first double-decker on Clapton Road.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the bus with old reggae tunes. Even the driver was smiling. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I sat in a café on Weserstrasse and heard a heated debate between a Turkish grandmother and a hipster about the best döner in town.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop where the meat is grilled to order while locals debate philosophy over their 3am currywurst.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a true local when they know the exact taco truck that serves the only al pastor worth it at 2 am, no google maps needed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a rider singing opera on the 30 Stockton last night. Most of the crowd looked annoyed, but a few were vibing along. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just a trendy spot, but they miss the quiet corners where locals sip café amb llet in peace, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They stand out with their maps in hand, trying to navigate the labyrinthine streets after dark, completely unaware of the shortcuts locals use.
